evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only requires nonempty, different manager PIDs and invocation IDs; it never checks that both manager observations happened on the same boot. A guest reboot between the manager restart and the second inspect can change both the manager PID and invocation ID, so the check reports an isolated manager restart even though the observations span a boot change. Requiring nonempty equal boot IDs in the manager before/after snapshots, while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks, is the smallest compatible correctness fix.
